product_offering.core_offering: Boulevard is an AI-driven SaaS client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses including salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, nail salons, and massage businesses. The unified platform combines Precision Scheduling AI, client management (CRM), POS/payments, marketing automation, memberships, loyalty programs, and reporting in a single subscription. For medspas, the platform adds HIPAA-compliant clinical charting and ePrescribe (powered by ScriptSure). The company also sells Boulevard Duo EMV-certified POS hardware and offers Enterprise-tier open APIs for custom integrations.
product_offering.differentiator: All-in-one client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses (not generic POS or legacy EMRs); AI-powered Precision Scheduling™; native payfac payments eliminating third-party processors; HIPAA-compliant charting and ePrescribe in a single system; self-booking overlays that stay on the business's own website and social channels; instant payouts and multi-merchant account support for independent contractors. The platform serves over 40,000 self-care professionals and processes ~$5B in payments annually.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Reduces scheduling gaps and optimizes calendar utilization; eliminates system switching between booking, charting, prescribing, and payments; increases client retention through personalized CRM and loyalty programs; streamlines checkout with integrated POS and contactless tipping; provides real-time business intelligence and flexible reporting; supports multi-location and franchise management with granular permissions; enables HIPAA-compliant patient documentation and EPCS-compliant e-prescribing.
product_offering.problem_solved: Fragmented technology stacks (separate booking, CRM, POS, marketing, and clinical systems); legacy EMRs not designed for luxury self-care client experiences; high no-show rates and scheduling inefficiencies; poor online booking experiences causing client abandonment; complex multi-location and franchise management; HIPAA and compliance requirements for medspas; payment processing friction and delayed payouts.
quantifiable_outcome: Salons using Boulevard's scheduling software saw more services booked, fewer no-shows and late cancellations, more retail value, and more gratuity (T+90 days)
Businesses switching to Boulevard saw average impact of 0% more revenue, more membership sales, more online booking, more service sales (12-month average, per medspa customer data)
Multi-location customers saw fewer no-shows and late cancellations within one year
67% of Gen Z and 64% of millennials have abandoned a salon due to clunky online booking; Boulevard's seamless self-booking addresses this directly
Memberships generate an average of 72% of income for leading self-care businesses; Boulevard's membership tools support this revenue stream
Over 70% of consumers prefer online booking; Boulevard's self-booking tools address this demand
Barbershop owners save up to 30 hours per month using Boulevard's appointment software
product_offering.product_overview: Boulevard is an AI-driven SaaS client experience platform for appointment-based self-care businesses (salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, nail salons, massage). The unified platform consists of a core system combining scheduling (Precision Scheduling), client management (CRM), POS/payments (Boulevard Payments with Duo hardware), marketing (email/SMS suite), and reporting. Additional modules include ePrescribe for medical prescribing, Boulevard AI for smart scheduling and automation, Memberships & Packages, Capital financing, and Forms & Charts for clinical documentation. The platform is offered across business sizes from individual salons to multi-location and enterprise operations, with Open API available for Enterprise tier customers.

recent_move.description: Closed an $80 million Series D led by JMI Equity at a ~$800 million post-money valuation, bringing total funding to ~$188 million, with proceeds earmarked for AI development and enterprise-grade features.

Launched Boulevard ePrescribe via partnership with D.A.W. Systems (ScriptSure), embedding electronic prescribing for controlled, non-controlled, and compounded medications directly into the medspa workflow.
Closed a $70 million Series C led by Point72 Private Investments to fund platform development, vertical expansion (into medspas), and engineering headcount growth.
Launched Boulevard AI, an AI feature suite encompassing smart scheduling, automated client communications, personalization, and chatbot capabilities for the beauty and wellness vertical.

Partnered with D.A.W. Systems to operationalize EPCS-compliant e-prescribing and expanded enterprise integrations including Snowflake Data Share, Okta SSO, and OPERA PMS to capture franchise and enterprise self-care brands.

expansion_highlight.description: Medspa vertical penetration at ~15% of US medspas signals a focused go-to-market push into clinical/HIPAA-regulated workflows, supported by a $500–$600/location/month add-on layer that expands average revenue per account.

Series D (July 2025) proceeds explicitly allocated to AI tools and enterprise-grade features, including Open APIs, Snowflake Data Share, and advanced permissions, indicating an upmarket push into franchise and enterprise self-care brands.
April 2026 launch of ePrescribe via ScriptSure/D.A.W. Systems extends the product surface into electronic prescribing for controlled substances, opening EPCS-compliant revenue per medspa provider.

2025 launch of Boulevard AI (smart scheduling, automated messaging, personalization, chatbots) is a product-line expansion that monetizes the existing data flywheel across 40,000+ professionals and $5B in payments.

Distribution expansion through Reserve with Google, Facebook/Instagram Book Now, and Zapier integrations enables product-led client acquisition and embeds Boulevard into consumer discovery channels, reducing dependence on direct sales.

Add-on modules such as Boulevard Capital (business financing) and Boulevard Duo hardware extend monetization beyond subscription into financial services and hardware, increasing customer LTV within the existing base.

company_assessment.market_position: Boulevard is a privately held, AI-driven SaaS client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses including salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, nail salons, and massage businesses. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, the company serves more than 40,000 self-care professionals, processes approximately $5 billion in payments annually, and now powers approximately 15% of U.S. medspas. Following an $80 million Series D round led by JMI Equity in July 2025, the company is valued at approximately $800 million and has raised approximately $188 million in total funding across rounds led by Point72 Private Investments, Index Ventures, Toba Capital, and Bonfire Ventures.

strengths.details: At ~15% of US medspas today, Boulevard is in early innings of a HIPAA/EPCS-required vertical with higher willingness-to-pay than salons. Medspa add-ons at $500-$600/location/month expand ARPU and the ePrescribe launch (April 2026) creates a clinical lock-in that should compound into higher enterprise contracts and lower churn over time.
strengths.headline: Medspa expansion unlocks much larger clinical TAM

strengths.details: Processing ~$5B in annual payment volume through a native payfac means Boulevard earns a transaction fee on every dollar that flows through its 40,000+ professionals. As the customer base grows and per-location volume expands (especially with medspa add-ons), payment revenue compounds without proportional sales investment.
strengths.headline: Payments flywheel scales transaction revenue with no incremental CAC

strengths.details: Precision Scheduling™ and Boulevard AI are trained on aggregated booking and $5B payment data from 40,000+ professionals. This proprietary dataset enables personalization and recommendation features that improve with scale, making Boulevard's AI offering structurally harder to replicate by new entrants or generalist competitors.
strengths.headline: AI moat deepens with proprietary booking and transaction data

strengths.details: Boulevard has signed enterprise customers (TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday) and is gating API access, Snowflake Data Share, and advanced permissions behind the Enterprise tier. As the multi-location customer count grows, average contract value should expand materially and pull-through payments, ePrescribe, and Capital financing attach.
strengths.headline: Enterprise and franchise tier drives contract size expansion

strengths.details: The Capital add-on lets Boulevard underwrite or facilitate financing to its existing customer base, monetizing trust and cash-flow data already on the platform. This creates a high-margin fintech layer on top of SaaS and payments with low incremental customer acquisition cost.
strengths.headline: Embedded fintech (Capital) opens new revenue stream from same customers

weakness.details: Mindbody, Fresha (free core product), and Square Appointments (bundled with payments) compete on price and ecosystem breadth. As they push deeper into medspas, Boulevard may face pricing pressure and elevated CAC that compress the path-to-profitability and force discounting at renewal.
weakness.headline: Aggressive incumbents compress pricing and win rates

weakness.details: Serving medspas with HIPAA, EPCS, and clinical charting obligations increases product, security, and support overhead compared to plain salon software. As regulatory expectations evolve (e.g., controlled substance prescribing rules), Boulevard's engineering and compliance resources may be diverted from core salon/spa roadmap, weakening the broader platform.
weakness.headline: Medspa compliance burden could slow product velocity

weakness.details: ePrescribe is delivered through D.A.W. Systems' ScriptSure under a partnership arrangement. Any deterioration in the relationship, partner-side outages, regulatory action against the prescriber network, or unfavorable contract renewal terms directly undermine Boulevard's medspa differentiation and could force costly in-house development.
weakness.headline: Third-party ePrescribe dependency threatens medspa expansion

weakness.details: All revenue is tied to US self-care businesses — a discretionary consumer category. In an economic downturn, average ticket size, visit frequency, and new location openings contract, which directly reduces both SaaS seat revenue and transaction-fee volume from Boulevard Payments.
weakness.headline: Concentration in discretionary US self-care exposes to downturns

weakness.details: The Series D funds expanded enterprise sales, onboarding, and AI features. Enterprise contracts have longer sales cycles and higher service costs than SMB; if enterprise mix grows faster than SMB volume, near-term margins and cash efficiency could deteriorate before enterprise renewal economics kick in.
weakness.headline: Enterprise expansion burn may pressure unit economics before scale

competitive_moat.details: Boulevard's platform embeds memberships, client purchase history, payment processing, clinical charting, and e-prescribing into a single workflow. Once a salon, medspa, or franchise standardizes operations, payment routing, and clinical documentation on Boulevard, migrating that data and re-wiring integrations creates significant operational disruption.

Proprietary Precision Scheduling AI algorithm and the native Boulevard Payments payfac are purpose-built for appointment-based self-care workflows rather than adapted from generic POS/EMR software. The combination of a custom scheduling engine and a vertically-integrated payment stack is difficult for horizontal SaaS players to replicate quickly.

HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, EPCS, and Level 1 PCI certifications are required to serve medspas handling PHI and controlled substances, creating a compliance barrier for new entrants. Boulevard's ePrescribe integration (D.A.W. Systems/ScriptSure) is also operationalized across 30,000+ prescribers nationwide.

Boulevard aggregates behavioral data from 40,000+ self-care professionals and approximately $5 billion in annual payment volume, which feeds the Precision Scheduling algorithm and marketing personalization. This dataset compounds with scale and improves AI quality over time.

Boulevard's native payfac eliminates third-party processor dependencies, while Open APIs (Admin, Client, Credit Card Tokenization, Report Export) at the Enterprise tier create integration stickiness with ERPs, Snowflake, Okta SSO, OPERA PMS, Shopify, and QuickBooks. Hardware (Boulevard Duo) and the Capital financing add-on further entrench customers.

key_risks.details: Boulevard's operations are explicitly domestic USA-only with no global footprint claim. This concentrates risk in a single market and limits TAM relative to international peers like Treatwell or Phorest.
key_risks.headline: US-only geographic concentration limits addressable market

key_risks.details: The self-care booking space includes Mindbody, Vagaro, Fresha, Square Appointments, Booksy, GlossGenius, Zenoti, and Mangomint. Several competitors are VC-backed and price aggressively (Fresha is free for core), pressuring win rates and pricing.
key_risks.headline: Crowded competitive landscape with well-funded incumbents and pure-plays

key_risks.details: Boulevard's new medspa ePrescribe feature is powered entirely by D.A.W. Systems' ScriptSure. Any disruption to this partnership, pricing change, or compliance failure at the partner level directly impacts Boulevard's medspa expansion thesis.
key_risks.headline: Dependency on D.A.W. Systems / ScriptSure for ePrescribe functionality

key_risks.details: Serving medspas requires HIPAA, EPCS, and clinical charting compliance plus medical director workflows — a meaningful operational lift. Compliance failures could trigger regulatory exposure and reputational damage that affect the broader platform.
key_risks.headline: Medspa regulatory complexity raises execution and compliance risk

key_risks.details: Matt Danna (Co-Founder & CEO) is the single named executive with detailed visibility; only a handful of additional leaders (CTO, CFO, CMO) are surfaced. Concentrated founder dependency and limited public detail on the broader bench create succession and execution risk.
key_risks.headline: Key-person dependency on founder-CEO with thin disclosed leadership bench

key_risks.details: Salon, spa, and medspa demand is correlated with discretionary consumer spending. A consumer downturn would directly reduce bookings, payment volume, and customer retention — Boulevard's transaction-fee and subscription revenue are both exposed.
key_risks.headline: Self-care vertical cyclicality tied to discretionary consumer spend

key_highlights.details: Per company materials, Boulevard now serves 40,000+ self-care professionals (up from 25,000 in 2,000 locations at the 2022 Series C) and powers approximately 15% of US medspas, indicating rapid customer growth and vertical penetration.
key_highlights.headline: Strong traction: 40,000+ self-care professionals and ~15% US medspa market share

key_highlights.details: JMI Equity-led $80M Series D in July 2025 valued Boulevard at ~$800M with ~$188M total raised. The platform processes ~$5B in payments annually, indicating significant scale relative to capital deployed.
key_highlights.headline: $800M valuation on $188M cumulative funding and $5B annual payment volume

key_highlights.details: Revenue streams include SaaS subscriptions (medspa add-ons at $500-$600/location/month), transaction fees through Boulevard Payments™ native payfac, and Boulevard Duo™ EMV-certified POS hardware sales, reducing dependency on any single stream.
key_highlights.headline: Diversified revenue model combining SaaS subscription, payment processing, and hardware

key_highlights.details: Certifications across data security (SOC 2 Type 2), healthcare (HIPAA), payments (PCI Level 1), and controlled substance prescribing (EPCS) enable Boulevard to credibly serve medspa and clinical-aesthetics customers where generalist competitors fall short.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade compliance stack: SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, PCI Level 1, EPCS

key_highlights.details: Enterprise customers include TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, and Heyday, demonstrating credibility with multi-location and franchise brands where contract sizes and switching costs are larger.
key_highlights.headline: Strong enterprise and franchise logos: TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday

key_highlights.details: Boulevard combines scheduling (Precision Scheduling™ AI), CRM, POS, marketing, ePrescribe, and payments in one stack, eliminating the fragmented toolset typical of salon/spa operators. The native payfac eliminates third-party processors.
key_highlights.headline: Differentiated all-in-one platform with native payfac and AI scheduling

key_highlights.details: Named to the 2024 Deloitte Technology Fast 500 and recognized as 'Best Value 2025' by Capterra and on G2, providing third-party credibility on growth and customer satisfaction.
key_highlights.headline: External validation: Deloitte Fast 500, Capterra Best Value, G2 recognition

customer_concentration.details: Customer base is broad with 40,000+ self-care professionals served across an estimated thousands of business locations, suggesting a long-tail, volume-driven model rather than reliance on a small number of anchor contracts. Named enterprise and franchise logos (TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday) indicate Boulevard is winning flagship multi-location brands, but these appear as reference accounts rather than dominant revenue contributors. The vertical segmentation (medspas, salons, spas, barbershops, nail, massage) and explicit SMB/mid-market/enterprise tiering further distribute exposure. Overall concentration risk is Low to Moderate: enterprise wins support marketing credibility, but no single logo appears to materially drive revenue.
